title: Canvas Basics
summary: Draw pixels and shapes into a region controlled by JavaScript.
nestedConcepts: Redraw after size or state changes

subtopics.title: Set canvas drawing dimensions
subtopics.explanation: The `<canvas>` element defines a drawing area. Set its width and height attributes for the drawing resolution, then use CSS for its displayed size. It is like choosing both the grid on graph paper and the paper’s size. If those sizes differ, account for scaling so the drawing stays crisp.

subtopics.title: Draw with the 2D context
subtopics.explanation: A 2D context provides commands for drawing shapes, text, and images. JavaScript obtains it with `canvas.getContext("2d")`. It is like choosing the drawing tools before starting. Check that the context exists, and keep drawing logic separate from unrelated page behavior.

subtopics.title: Canvas
subtopics.explanation: Canvas coordinates start at the top-left: x grows to the right and y grows downward. It is like a map whose origin is the upper-left corner. A point at x=20 and y=10 sits near that corner. Use the coordinate system consistently when placing shapes.

subtopics.title: Redraw
subtopics.explanation: Canvas does not redraw automatically when application data changes. Clear and redraw the scene when values, size, or animation state changes. It is like refreshing a whiteboard after its information changes. Keep the source data outside the pixels so the drawing can be recreated.

subtopics.title: Provide an accessible HTML alternative
subtopics.explanation: Canvas pixels are not exposed like ordinary headings, labels, and buttons. Provide an equivalent explanation in HTML, and use real HTML controls for actions. It is like showing a chart while also stating its key findings in words. Important information must remain available to assistive technology.

foundations.overview: The `<canvas>` element gives JavaScript a blank area for drawing pixels, shapes, charts, or animation. The drawing itself is not ordinary HTML text, so screen readers may not understand it automatically. Think of canvas like a sheet of graph paper: JavaScript draws marks at measured coordinates. Use it for custom visuals, and provide text or controls that explain important information and actions.
foundations.whyItMatters: Canvas is useful when an application needs custom pixel drawing or animation. It also shifts responsibility for scaling, redraws, and accessible alternatives to the developer.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Canvas is like a blank sheet where your code paints every mark.
commonUseCases: Draw a chart or game surface with many changing pixels.
Resize a drawing while preserving its coordinate system.
Offer an accessible text summary and HTML controls beside the drawing.
Draw a simple game board whose positions change after each move.
Display a custom chart while providing a nearby data table.
Resize a drawing and redraw it using the application’s source data.
Keep the chart’s key value available in text if canvas drawing is unsupported.
Use SVG when a diagram needs individually focusable or named shapes.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Canvas drawings are exposed like ordinary HTML text.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Pixels do not provide the same semantic information; provide text alternatives and controls.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Canvas automatically redraws when data changes.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Application code must draw again when its data, size, or state changes.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Canvas is the right choice for every diagram.
commonMisconceptions.reality: HTML and SVG often offer more accessible structure for ordinary diagrams and interface graphics.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Canvas content is automatically readable to a screen reader.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Pixels do not expose the same structure as HTML; provide a text explanation and usable controls.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Changing a data value updates the drawing automatically.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Application code must redraw when data or size changes.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Canvas is the best way to make an ordinary icon.
commonMisconceptions.reality: SVG or HTML often provides sharper, more accessible structure for simple graphics.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A title attribute makes a complex canvas chart accessible.
commonMisconceptions.reality: Important chart meaning needs an accessible text equivalent, not only a tooltip or title.

keyTakeaways: The `<canvas>` element defines a drawing area.
A 2D context provides commands for drawing shapes, text, and images.
Canvas coordinates start at the top-left: x grows to the right and y grows downward.
Canvas does not redraw automatically when application data changes.
Canvas pixels are not exposed like ordinary headings, labels, and buttons.
